To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the precision of QTL mapping with the LDLA approaches depends on the number of families and the size of families; (ii) the LDLA_reg method is more accurate for QTL position estimation than the LDLA_vc method, but requires much less computing time; (iii) in the case of a sparse map, the LDLA approaches are better than the Haley–Knott regression (HK_reg); and (iv) the precision of LDLA_reg and HK_reg is very similar

the precision of the LDLA_reg method is not influenced by population size, that a small number of families is sufficient to obtain a good precision of QTL location, that increasing the number of progeny per sire improves precision of QTL estimation and that the LDLA_vc method is more computationally expensive than the LDLA_regression method.

(1) the use of a medium-density marker panel is efficient for QTL mapping; (2) the use of half-sib progenies is recommended, but the use of a small number of full-sib families is also possible; (3) the use of the LDLA_reg approach is recommended, as it is more accurate and faster than the LDLA_vc approach; (4) for a medium-density marker set, the LDLA_reg is not significantly less accurate than a dense marker set
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of different linkage disequilibrium (LD) linkage analysis models and the influence of population structure on the precision of QTL mapping.
the efficiency of population structures for QTL mapping and the comparison of the two LDLA approaches.
the accuracy of QTL mapping in the case of a medium-density marker panel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number of half-sib progeny per sire is more critical than the number of families.
for the QTL position estimation, the number of progeny per sire is more important than the number of families.
the number of half-sib progenies per sire should be maximized, and that the number of families should be minimized, without reducing the total number of individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the LDLA_reg approach, with the use of a medium-density marker panel, could be used to map QTLs with a high precision, especially in sparse map situations, and the precision was not significantly affected by the number of families.
the number of families and the size of each family should be considered together to achieve the highest accuracy in the QTL position estimation.
the number of progeny per sire is a key factor in the precision of QTL location, while the number of families is of less importance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of half-sib progenies is a good strategy to detect QTLs in a dense map situation.
for a fixed number of individuals in the mapping population, the use of a few large full- and half- sib families is preferable for fine-mapping QTLs.
, when using a dense marker map, the LDLA_reg method is the most efficient approach to map QTLs, whereas, when a medium density map is used, the LDLA_vc method is more efficient.
